newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Yuganskneftegaz won't pump more oil soon.
newsitem.headline: Russian Yuganskneftegaz won't pump more oil soon.

text.p: Russia's big Yuganskneftegaz oil production company will not see any increases in crude oil output soon, the firm controlling the major producer said on Thursday.

"We do not plan to increase (oil) production," Mikhail Khodorkovsky, chief executive of the Rosprom-YUKOS holding company, which controls the producer, told the Sevodnya daily newspaper. He did not specify a time horizon.
"The current level of oil production and refining at our plants will be maintained. We will continue work on cutting expenses and increasing refining efficiency," Sevodnya quoted him as saying.
Yuganskneftegaz is the main production unit of vertically-integrated YUKOS, Russia's second largest integrated oil company.

YUKOS President Sergei Muravlenko estimated in February that Yuganskneftegaz's 1997 output would be 25.2 million tonnes (504,000 barrels per day) after an estimated 26.38 million (527,600 bpd) tonnes in 1996.
He estimated Yukos 1997 production would be 33.2 million tonnes (664,000 bpd) and Yukos 1997 refining would rise to 21.66 million tonnes (433,200 bpd), a 17.3 percent increase on 1996 levels.
Sevodnya quoted Khodorovsky as saying petrochemicals and sales would be important to company growth.

"I would not say that petrochemicals is the most profitable of all the ways to use oil," he said. "But I think that it is the shortest and most accessible path to company growth, one where we can use the experience and education of management."
He reconfirmed that Rosprom-YUKOS would chose an investment bank at the end of May to secure financing for medium- and long-term projects.
